cohort: 384 term and apparently healthy neonates born at University of Gondar Hospital, Gondar Town, Northwest Ethiopia, in 2018
finding: Male neonates have a significantly larger anterior fontanelle size than female neonates at term, and anterior fontanelle size is positively correlated with birth weight and head circumference.
mod_finding: Anterior fontanelle size differed significantly between neonates born vaginally and those born by caesarean section.
